purpose: Exact ordered procedure for the parent (owner) session to execute the four remaining US-005 live gates inside the accepted US-007 Docker sbx workload profile: (a) empty_rust_target_fails, (b) planted_java_rust_mutants_killed, (c) sealed_network_denial, (d) execution_rerun_reconciliation. This plan performs NO sbx runs and NO live recording itself.

target_platform.sbx: Docker sbx CLI v0.39.0 (pinned commit def8cb0523a77e757bdd6ef52b459fe374f3783e, protected/us007-resource-supervisor/sbx_validation.go)
target_platform.os_arch: linux/arm64 (US-007 supervisor binaries are -linux-arm64; template ships Debian go1.26.0 linux/arm64 at /usr/bin/go per supervisor.go probed constants)
target_platform.profile_constraints: no shared skills, no local MCP, no secrets, no protected-store mounts; owner-authorized per attempt (us007-attempt-XXXX-owner-authorization.json pattern)

spend_semantics.public_tier: custodian-free: cmd/corporactl/main.go:217-219 defines heldOutTier(tier) as tier==hidden||tier==sealed; oracle-requests spends only inside 'if heldOutTier(*tier)' (main.go:268-282) and evaluate likewise (main.go:326-334). Public and handshake invocations never open the ledger.
spend_semantics.oracle_requests_held_out: spends 1 query keyed by sha256('oracle-requests|'+tier+'|'+all request lines) (main.go:274-278). The digest is deterministic for a fixed corpus+epoch, so EVERY re-emission repeats the SAME digest. Both held-out digests already sit at 2 of the 3-repeat threshold; one more emission on either tier permanently latches the custodian (internal/corpora/custodian.go:241-262).
spend_semantics.evaluate_held_out: spends 1 query keyed by sha256('evaluate|'+tier+'|'+transcript bytes) BEFORE any expectation is consulted (main.go:326-334). A byte-different transcript is a NEW digest with count 1 — candidate transcripts (stub, mutants) differ from the oracle's and from each other, so their first evaluations are fresh digests and carry no probing risk. Identical bytes repeat the digest: count 2 on the second evaluation, LATCH on the third (custodian.go:227-262; counts are per-digest via queryCounts, custodian.go:241).
spend_semantics.diagnostics_held_out: when a held-out evaluation has failures, corporactl automatically attempts one diagnostic spend keyed by sha256('diagnostics|'+tier+'|'+transcript) to include failure details, redacting them if denied (main.go:361-376). RecordDiagnostic does NOT feed the probing counter (custodian.go:274-296 never touches queryCounts; LoadLedger counts only op=='query' entries, custodian.go:343-345). Every killed candidate on a held-out tier therefore costs 1 query + 1 diagnostic.
spend_semantics.atomicity: SpendCustodian flock-serializes load-spend-persist and persists denial entries (internal/corpora/spend.go:12-37), so every attempt lands in the hash-chained ledger even when denied.
spend_semantics.worst_case_budget_this_plan: stub 2q + 4 mutants x 2 tiers = 8q + diagnostics <=10 + optional rerun evaluations <=10q => <=20 of 192 queries, <=10 of 50 diagnostics. Ample; budget is not the risk — identical-digest repetition is.

hard_prohibitions: NEVER run corporactl oracle-requests --tier hidden or --tier sealed again in epoch 1: both digests are at 2 of 3; a third identical invocation permanently latches the custodian until rotation. REUSE the recorded requests files instead.

NEVER run corporactl evaluate --tier hidden with any transcript byte-identical to protected/us005-corpora/live/hidden/transcript.jsonl, and likewise for sealed: those evaluate digests are also at 2 of 3 and a third identical evaluation latches. sha256-compare any transcript against the recorded oracle transcripts BEFORE evaluating it on a held-out tier.
NEVER evaluate the same candidate transcript bytes a third time on a held-out tier: the first evaluation takes its digest to 1, an identical rerun evaluation to 2 — stop there.

NEVER mount or copy the protected store, the custodian secret, or the scenarios/expectations into the sandbox: candidates receive ONLY requests.jsonl files (inputs); all evaluation happens outside the sandbox.

NEVER publish sandbox outputs without a canary sweep: held-out requests embed secret-derived canary tokens; transcripts echo request material. All held-out transcripts stay in the protected store; run DetectCanaryLeak semantics over anything public.

requests_reuse.public: protected/us005-corpora/live/public/requests.jsonl (sha256 0c1503c043172d09... — verified byte-identical to a fresh custodian-free public emission in evidence/us005-candidate-public-proof.json)

steps.name: owner-authorization
commands: mint a fresh us005 candidate-execution attempt authorization following the us007-attempt-XXXX-owner-authorization.json pattern (owner-signed, per attempt)
steps.notes: executions/US-007.json constraints record generic_sbx_live_reruns_permitted:false and fresh_generic_sbx_attempts_remaining:0 for US-007's OWN envelope-validation workload. US-005 candidate execution is a different workload under the same accepted profile, but it is still owner-authorized per attempt — the parent must decide/mint this explicitly, not inherit it from this plan.

steps.name: cross-compile linux/arm64 candidate binaries (host)
commands: GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -trimpath -o out/us005-netprobe-linux-arm64 ./cmd/us005-netprobe
rustup target add aarch64-unknown-linux-musl --toolchain 1.95.0-aarch64-apple-darwin
cd rust && RUSTFLAGS='-C linker=rust-lld -C link-self-contained=yes' cargo build --release -p candidate-stub --target aarch64-unknown-linux-musl
file rust/target/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/release/us005-candidate-stub  # expect: statically linked ELF aarch64
steps.notes: Both paths were probed live on 2026-08-26 and produce statically linked ELF aarch64 binaries (evidence/us005-candidate-public-proof.json cross_compilation_probe). Static musl linking avoids any glibc dependency on the Debian template.

steps.name: build java mutant jars (host; bytecode is platform-independent)
commands: go build -o out/us005-mutantctl ./cmd/us005-mutantctl
out/us005-mutantctl stage --pristine java-oracle/src/main/java --overlay mutants/java/us005-jm-close-code-1000 --out out/jm-close-code-1000
out/us005-mutantctl build --staged out/jm-close-code-1000 --java-websocket-jar <pinned Java-WebSocket-1.6.0.jar, verify sha256 eae29213e4f16515639c28957200f011b3967fffcada1962cf0255d24919c22f>
out/us005-mutantctl stage --pristine java-oracle/src/main/java --overlay mutants/java/us005-jm-utf8-accept --out out/jm-utf8-accept
out/us005-mutantctl build --staged out/jm-utf8-accept --java-websocket-jar <same pinned jar>

steps.name: create the sandbox (accepted profile shape)
commands: sbx version                          # must equal 'sbx version: v0.39.0 def8cb0523a77e757bdd6ef52b459fe374f3783e'
sbx daemon status --json             # must report running

sbx create --clone --cpus 2 --memory 2g --deny-network '**' --name us005-cand-<attempt> --template docker.io/docker/sandbox-templates:shell@sha256:1e642f7fadebcbff3d8de67114e9b42a5971ba9b4287ebffa1d05662f5a0f5ec shell <clean source clone>
sbx inspect us005-cand-<attempt> --json
sbx policy ls us005-cand-<attempt> --json
sbx policy check network --sandbox us005-cand-<attempt> example.com --json   # host-side deny confirmation
steps.notes: argv shape lifted from the accepted US-007 operator (protected/us007-resource-supervisor/operator.go:36,160-186). Candidate execution needs NO --privileged and NO root: candidates are plain stdin/stdout workloads.

steps.name: deliver candidates and requests into the sandbox
commands: sbx exec us005-cand-<attempt> sh -c 'mkdir -p /us005/bin /us005/requests /us005/out'
sbx cp out/us005-netprobe-linux-arm64 us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/bin/us005-netprobe
sbx cp rust/target/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/release/us005-candidate-stub us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/bin/us005-candidate-stub
sbx cp rust/target/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/release/us005-mutant-rs-eager-reject us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/bin/us005-mutant-rs-eager-reject
sbx cp rust/target/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/release/us005-mutant-rs-digest-unbind us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/bin/us005-mutant-rs-digest-unbind
sbx cp out/jm-close-code-1000/java-oracle-mutant.jar us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/bin/jm-close-code-1000.jar
sbx cp out/jm-utf8-accept/java-oracle-mutant.jar us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/bin/jm-utf8-accept.jar
sbx cp <pinned Java-WebSocket-1.6.0.jar> us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/bin/Java-WebSocket-1.6.0.jar
sbx cp <pinned slf4j-api-2.0.13.jar> us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/bin/slf4j-api-2.0.13.jar
sbx cp protected/us005-corpora/live/public/requests.jsonl us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/requests/public.jsonl
sbx cp protected/us005-corpora/live/hidden/requests.jsonl us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/requests/hidden.jsonl
sbx cp protected/us005-corpora/live/sealed/requests.jsonl us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/requests/sealed.jsonl
steps.notes: requests files are candidate INPUTS only (scenario steps); expectations, secrets, ledger, and canary inventory never enter the sandbox. Copying specific request files is not a protected-store mount.

steps.name: PROBE_BEFORE_WIRE: smoke the execution path and the java runtime
commands: sbx exec us005-cand-<attempt> /us005/bin/us005-candidate-stub --identify   # expect the identity JSON line
sbx exec us005-cand-<attempt> sh -c 'command -v java || echo NO_JAVA'
sbx exec us005-cand-<attempt> sh -c 'printf %s\\n "{}" | /us005/bin/us005-candidate-stub'   # stdin/stdout piping smoke
steps.notes: If NO_JAVA: materialize a pinned linux/aarch64 JDK 17 archive ON THE HOST (record source URL + sha256 at fetch time per probe-before-wire; do NOT trust this plan for the URL), sbx cp it in, and invoke java from that path. If the owner declines JDK materialization, record the java-mutant half of the gate as BLOCKED rather than running mutants outside the sandbox.

steps.name: execution 1: run every candidate on every behavior tier inside the sandbox
commands: for tier in public hidden sealed: sbx exec us005-cand-<attempt> sh -c '/us005/bin/us005-candidate-stub < /us005/requests/$tier.jsonl > /us005/out/stub-$tier-1.jsonl'
... same loop for us005-mutant-rs-eager-reject and us005-mutant-rs-digest-unbind ...

for tier in public hidden sealed: sbx exec us005-cand-<attempt> sh -c 'java -Dslf4j.internal.verbosity=ERROR -cp /us005/bin/jm-close-code-1000.jar:/us005/bin/Java-WebSocket-1.6.0.jar:/us005/bin/slf4j-api-2.0.13.jar OracleMain < /us005/requests/$tier.jsonl > /us005/out/jm-close-code-1000-$tier-1.jsonl'
... same loop for jm-utf8-accept ...
steps.notes: Mutant jars pass the oracle's startup runtime-digest verification because the pinned library jar rides alongside; only OracleEngine is mutated.

steps.name: sealed_network_denial gate: probe DURING the sealed-tier window
commands: sbx exec us005-cand-<attempt> sh -c '/us005/bin/us005-netprobe > /us005/out/netprobe-1.json; echo exit=$?'   # run between/alongside the sealed-tier candidate runs, inside the same sandbox
sbx policy check network --sandbox us005-cand-<attempt> example.com --json   # host-side corroboration
steps.expected: exit=0 and verdict network_denied:true with every attempt denied. The probe's host self-test (exit 1, all connected — evidence/us005-candidate-public-proof.json netprobe_selftest) proves it genuinely discriminates open networks.
steps.notes: gate evidence = in-sandbox verdict JSON + host-side policy check + the create-time --deny-network '**' argv.

steps.name: extract transcripts and evaluate OUTSIDE the sandbox
commands: sbx cp us005-cand-<attempt>:/us005/out/. <protected-out>/us005-cand-<attempt>/

PRE-CHECK (mandatory): shasum -a 256 each held-out transcript and compare against protected/us005-corpora/live/{hidden,sealed}/transcript.jsonl — if any candidate transcript is byte-identical to a recorded oracle transcript, STOP: evaluating it would be that digest's third occurrence and latches the custodian. (No inert/mutant candidate can legitimately reproduce the oracle transcript; identity means something is wrong.)
corporactl evaluate --root <repo> --protected-root <orchestrator protected root> --tier public --transcript <each candidate public transcript>    # custodian-free
corporactl evaluate ... --tier hidden --transcript <each candidate hidden transcript>    # 1 query + 1 diagnostic each, fresh digests
corporactl evaluate ... --tier sealed --transcript <each candidate sealed transcript>    # 1 query + 1 diagnostic each, fresh digests
steps.expected: stub: executed=74/92/92, passed=0, exit 1 per tier (empty_rust_target_fails). Mutants: exit 1 per tier with the kill signatures in mutants/manifest.json (public-tier measured: jm-close-code-1000 19 kills, jm-utf8-accept 2 kills, rs mutants 74/74). READ each report and exit code; a 0-exit or passed==executed on any candidate is a gate FAILURE to investigate, not to re-run blindly.

steps.name: execution 2 + execution_rerun_reconciliation gate
commands: repeat step 7 (and step 8) writing *-2.jsonl outputs — fresh sandbox from the same template digest is acceptable and preferred (us005-cand-<attempt+1>, new owner authorization)
sbx cp the second round out; shasum -a 256 every pair (candidate, tier): transcript-1 vs transcript-2

IF byte-identical (expected: all candidates are deterministic): record digest equality as the reconciliation proof. Do NOT evaluate the second identical transcript on held-out tiers unless the recorded gate schema demands an evaluate-backed rerun; if it does, that second evaluation takes the digest to 2 of 3 — record that fact and NEVER evaluate those bytes again.
IF divergent: that is a flake — the gate FAILS reconciliation; evaluate the divergent transcript (fresh digest, safe) to characterize it, then investigate. Do not average or retry-until-identical.
steps.notes: This is the only step whose naive form (evaluate everything twice, then once more 'to be sure') reaches the latch. The digest-equality path keeps every candidate evaluate digest at count 1; the evaluate-backed path stops at 2. There is no safe third.

steps.name: record, sweep, and clean up
commands: write transcripts, reports, netprobe verdicts, and sbx receipts into protected/us005-corpora/live/ per the live-evidence schema; update evidence/corpus-calibration.json gates via the existing calibrate/verify flow

canary sweep: scan every artifact destined for the repo or any public surface against the canary token inventory (DetectCanaryLeak semantics, internal/corpora/custodian.go:388-399); held-out transcripts stay in the protected store
sbx rm us005-cand-<attempt>*

reconciliation_rules.definition: two live candidate executions reconcile iff for every (candidate, tier) the two transcripts are byte-identical (sha256 equality) AND every evaluation verdict (pass/fail counters and exit code) is identical between rounds
reconciliation_rules.oracle_half: already satisfied and recorded: the pinned oracle's two 2026-08-26 executions were byte-identical on all three tiers (requests-rerun and transcript-rerun files equal their originals)
reconciliation_rules.candidate_half: produced by steps 7-10; digest-equality is the preferred proof precisely because it is also the custodian-safe one
